task: Independent full-preset plucked-string and tuned-bar behavior review
scope: Development audio review; final native qualification and calibrated whole-bank acceptance are separate. No reference recordings or acoustic-equivalence claim.

capture.isolated_rank_override: Rank2 uses mix=1; digest recomputed after this explicit override.

methods.onset_peak_rms: Maximum stereo RMS over50ms windows with10ms hops inside0..300ms.
methods.onset_spectrum: Mono Hann-window FFT at20..200ms; harmonic bands ±max(12Hz,0.2% center) around the sounding primary. Upper means harmonics2..12 relative to harmonic1; amplitude normalization cancels.
methods.held_decay: Stereo RMS at2.2..2.8s relative to peak onset RMS; note held until3s.
methods.pitch_scope: All clips use played MIDI60. Kalimba main body sounds C5 due its4-foot registration; the other selected main bodies sound C4. These compare complete preset identities, not a controlled same-pitch resonator experiment.
methods.floor: RMS and dB displays floor at1e-12; late isolated strikes below this floor are reported as fully damped in that fixture, not precision physical decay measurements.

findings: Guitar II and Mandolin retain brighter normalized onset harmonic balances than Nylon Pluck at both tested velocities.
Guitar II rings longer than the paired, more compact Mandolin program.
Harp retains markedly more held energy than the high-register short Kalimba preset; Vibraphone retains more than Marimba.
Isolated supporting ranks are independently damped and do not create a sustained extra fundamental in the tested three-second holds.
All14 complete-preset captures and2 isolated-rank captures are finite and below full scale.
limits: One played key, two velocities and one deterministic render seed; this is not complete register or performance coverage.
Root was calibrating level tables; captured vectors/digests identify the actual fixtures independently of later master trims.
Energy/FFT differences support authored distinctions and articulation, not subjective preference or physical-instrument equivalence.
